From 80d3d33cdf4b0494b465087eb34d2e29d86e290e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Darrick J. Wong" <djwong@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2024 22:11:55 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] xfs: fix a memory leak

kmemleak reported that we don't free the parent pointer names here if we
found corruption.

Fixes: 0d29a20fbdba8 ("xfs: scrub parent pointers")
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <djwong@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Chandan Babu R <chandanbabu@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/xfs/scrub/parent.c b/fs/xfs/scrub/parent.c
index 733c410a2279..91e7b51ce068 100644
--- a/fs/xfs/scrub/parent.c
+++ b/fs/xfs/scrub/parent.c
@@ -799,7 +799,7 @@ xchk_parent_pptr(
 	}
 
 	if (pp->sc->sm->sm_flags & XFS_SCRUB_OFLAG_CORRUPT)
-		goto out_pp;
+		goto out_names;
 
 	/*
 	 * Complain if the number of parent pointers doesn't match the link
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `fs/xfs/scrub/parent.c`**
   - The line `goto out_pp;` was changed to `goto out_names;` within the `xchk_parent_pptr` function. This modification alters the control flow to ensure that if corruption is detected (indicated by the `XFS_SCRUB_OFLAG_CORRUPT` flag), the code will now jump to the `out_names` label instead of the `out_pp` label.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change in the `goto` statement is significant because it addresses a memory leak issue reported by `kmemleak`. By redirecting the flow to `out_names`, the code ensures that the parent pointer names are properly freed when corruption is detected, thus preventing the memory leak that would occur if the original `goto out_pp;` was executed. This modification is a direct fix to the bug introduced in a previous commit (0d29a20fbdba8) related to scrubbing parent pointers.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (pp->sc->sm->sm_flags & XFS_SCRUB_OFLAG_CORRUPT)
    goto out_names;
```
Reason:
This statement checks if the corruption flag is set and, if so, it jumps to the `out_names` label, which only frees the `pptr_names` but does not handle the cleanup of the parent pointer names, leading to a memory leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
goto out_names;
```
```c
goto out_pp;
```
Reason:
The fix changes the control flow to ensure that when corruption is detected, it properly jumps to the `out_names` label, which frees the allocated memory for `pptr_names`, thus preventing the memory leak that occurs when the corruption flag is set.
